LESSON: PLANE GEOMETRY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.1: Plane Geometry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Plane Geometry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are combined shapes applied in day-to-day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify instruments used in drawing
2. explain the layout of a drawing environment
3. construct combined shapes applied in drawing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PLANE GEOMETRY
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Plane Geometry helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

PART 1: Identify instruments used in drawing

What this means
In this part you learn to identify instruments used in drawing. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify instruments used in drawing.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Plane Geometry”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify instruments used in drawing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the layout of a drawing environment

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the layout of a drawing environment. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the layout of a drawing environment.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Plane Geometry.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the layout of a drawing environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Construct combined shapes applied in drawing

What this means
In this part you learn to construct combined shapes applied in drawing. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct combined shapes applied in drawing.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Check: Inspect your work and say one improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct combined shapes applied in drawing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Plane Geometry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Plane Geometry”. (skill: identify instruments used in drawing)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Plane Geometry. (skill: explain the layout of a drawing environment)

Example 3: Inspect your work and say one improvement. (skill: construct combined shapes applied in drawing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Plane Geometry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify instruments used in drawing.
3. Practise this skill: explain the layout of a drawing environment.
4. Practise this skill: construct combined shapes applied in drawing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Plane Geometry from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Plane Geometry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Plane Geometry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are combined shapes applied in day-to-day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Plane Geometry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify instruments used in drawing.
5. Be able to: explain the layout of a drawing environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
